summary: This note summarizes the St. Louis tenure of the franchise now known as the Los Angeles Rams, which played in St. Louis, Missouri, as the St. Louis Rams from 1995 through 2015. It covers the move from Los Angeles, the team's first and last home games in St. Louis, and its final game as a St. Louis-based club. The note is duplicated in the source.
one_line: Covers the St. Louis Rams era (1995-2015), including the team's first and last St. Louis home games and its final St. Louis-based game.
key_facts: The franchise now known as the Los Angeles Rams played in St. Louis, Missouri, as the St. Louis Rams from the 1995 through the 2015 seasons.
The team played in Los Angeles from the 1946 season to the 1994 season before relocating to St. Louis.
The franchise relocated from Los Angeles to St. Louis in 1995.
St. Louis had been without a National Football League (NFL) team since the Cardinals moved to Phoenix, Arizona, in 1988.
The Rams' first home game in St. Louis was at Busch Memorial Stadium against the New Orleans Saints on September 10, 1995.
The Trans World Dome was completed in time for the Rams' November 12 game against the Carolina Panthers.
The Trans World Dome was later known as the Edward Jones Dome and is now known as The Dome at America's Center.
The Rams' last game at the Edward Jones Dome was against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on December 17, 2015, which the Rams won 31-23.
The Rams' last game as a St. Louis-based club was on January 3, 2016, against the San Francisco 49ers at Levi's Stadium.
The Rams lost the January 3, 2016 game to the San Francisco 49ers in overtime, 19-16.
